moat_against: Ingrezza concentration: ~75% of revenue (Q2 2026 $716M of $959M) against an early-2030s patent cliff
Teva's Austedo XR is a real and growing VMAT2 competitor
Medicare / IRA price-negotiation overhang on a high-list-price specialty drug
Post-Ingrezza growth depends on binary 2027 Phase 3 readouts (osavampator MDD, direclidine schizophrenia) vs BMS Cobenfy in muscarinics
SBC runs ~26% of TTM OCF ($234.5M of $898.1M) with net dilution ~1.2%/yr
moat_for: Ingrezza patent exclusivity toward 2032 / generic insulation to ~2029, ~60% of new TD prescriptions, once-daily dosing vs Austedo
First-in-class monopoly positions in CAH (Crenessity) and Prader-Willi (Vykat XR)
~98% gross margins sustained FY2021-25 — proven pricing power
ROIC proxy 17.0% (2024) and 16.5% (2025), rising, despite a ~$2.5B low-yield cash pile in the capital base
Shared specialty commercial infrastructure across neurology and endocrinology lowers each launch's cost
moat_justification: Patent-protected first-in-class franchises (Ingrezza VMAT2, Crenessity CRF1, Vykat XR) with ~98% gross margins and ROIC proxy rising to 16.5-17.0% in 2024-25 (understated by a ~$2.5B cash/securities pile in the denominator), but Ingrezza is ~75% of revenue with exclusivity only into ~2029-2032, Austedo XR competes directly, and the post-cliff story rests on ramping launches plus binary 2027 Phase 3 readouts.
name: Neurocrine Biosciences, Inc.
one_liner: High-quality patent-moat biotech, moat 6/10 — just misses the 15% hurdle at $135.71 (weighted IRR 14.5%, IV@15% $128.80 on a $6.13 TTM base); clears 15% below ~$129, with 2027 pipeline readouts as the swing factor.
